prs.title: Deep links: the URL can say which slide, which panel, and where the cursor is
prs.head: deep-links

items.text: The selection in url seems useful. We already have a way to encode the slides contents into the url. I think doing it via name or via content have different semantics depending on the use case so it's quite hard to think though who would want what/when. This is probably more useful than just screenshots though. If we ever switch to cloudflare and can afford per-build deploys I think it would be great to encode commit sha, selection, and slide content into a url as that's actually reproducible.

The PanelRequest type in this file is the best pattern for this. I think we'd benefit from a type that represents the entire `DeepLink` request. Then separate out the "parsing"/"fetching" from the browser's query params from the logic that actually takes this and applies it to settings and the editor.

Ideally I think we would have this somewhat subsume the scratchpad url encoding so there would be a variant that either points to an existing slide by name/index or a new scratchpad by contents. Then the selection/sidebar stuff works as described.

items.text:
Not blocking, but I'm not sure `slide_name` belongs on `Globals`. It's Documentation-mode state, derived per frame in `Page.main_view`, living on an app-wide record so that one editor feature can read it. (It's also under `// State:` rather than `// Calculated:`.)

An alternative: `CodeEditable` only knows the span, so it could raise a global action carrying just that, e.g. `inject_global(CopyDeepLink(span))`, and let the Page-level update, which already knows the mode, the slide and the sidebar, build the URL and write it to the clipboard. That keeps the logic where the data lives and leaves `Globals.Model.t` unchanged.

It would also take care of `~linkable: bool`, which is currently `globals.slide_name != None` computed twice in `CodeEditable` and threaded through `get_sections` / `get_all_items` / `handle_listener_key` / `view`. If the menu took the `option` (or the Page level decided whether the row appears), the bare bool goes away.
items.evidence: 077a68f9f8: "slide_name leaves Globals: CodeEditable raises CopyDeepLink({position, text}) and the Page builds the link ... ~linkable leaves the context menu."

items.text: It's not clear to me why we default select the enclosing term as opposed to just sharing the caret position. I'm not opposed to it just unclear why

items.text: Feature works. Most feedback here is surface level but I think it deserves a once over before I approve. Biggest conceptual issue is we now have the scratch pad url encoding and this name-based documentation slide url encoding and they're completely separate and neither work in tutorial or other modes. Outside of that tests would be nice but possibly not necessary.

items.text:
@matthewhammer I can't easily comment on the draft page so just leaving stuff here. Lmk if you'd prefer something else.

```reason
type target =
  | Slide(string)                   /* ?slide=   a documentation slide, by name: a pointer */
  | Share(string, string);          /* ?name=&share=   a scratchpad's contents: a snapshot */
```
I think this would be better with constructors like `Documentation` and `Scratchpad`. Also maybe records instead of tuples for the stuff with multiple fields. Maybe the AI doesn't care but my human :brain: can't handle it.


```reason
type request = {
  target: option(target),
  panel: option(panel_request),     /* ?panel=  */
  position: option(position),
};
```
I'm not sure what situations we're expecting to be valid. But we might want a construction that doesn't allow target position without target.


The rest of this looks good :+1: :+1:
items.evidence: 077a68f9f8 uses constructors Documentation(string) and Scratchpad({name, text}) and a place = {target, position} type so a position cannot exist without a target ("A position only means something inside a target").

items.text:
🤖 I checked that nothing reads an elaboration's secondary. The only reader is `wrap_with_secondary` in `PreserveExact` mode, and `FastParse` is the only caller that sets that mode. Incremental reuse compares terms with `fast_equal` and `lexeme_trace`, neither of which looks at secondary, so reuse doesn't change either. The inline comments are small. The main issue is below.

### Some nodes still keep their secondary

The test checks that no expression or pattern keeps secondary, but its program is only a `let` and some arithmetic. I ran a temporary probe over the 72 programs in `hazel-programs/docs/reference` and `docs/b2t2`. It counted elaborated nodes of every kind that still carry secondary:

| kind | nodes |
|---|---|
| `typ` | 3,336 |
| `exp` | 506 |
| `tpat` | 132 |
| `pat` | 29 |
| `mod` | 2 |

Across the corpus, the marshaled elaborations are 1,065 KB as they are and 939 KB with secondary stripped from every node, so 13.5% is left. The table programs are hit hardest: `table-api-constructors-hcat.hz` is +44%, `errors-using-tables-browngetacne.hz` +43%, and `table-api-subtable-dropcolumn.hz` +38%.

The leftover secondary comes in through these paths:
- **Types:** `Typ.normali

prs.title: Statics: a module binding analyzes its definition once, not twice
prs.head: statics-module-def-once

items.text: This matches how labeled tuples work. I could see an argument to make incompatible signatures stuck but that's not how much of hazel works so I'm fine with this. In the signature sealing pr I have it would make y private.

items.text: @disconcision idk if you first added the module keyword but should this be an error defining a module to be a function?

items.text:
🤖 Preference, not blocking: these two blocks read as the history of the PR rather than a description of the code.

- The second block starts with "Unless…", so it only makes sense as a continuation of the first. One decision ends up described in two stacked comments.
- Both sit above `names_itself`, but the first is about the `def_elab_direct` lookup below it, hence "the one case below".
- Some of it belongs in the commit message: "not analyzed a second time", "every module binding cost twice what it should", "as before". After merge there's no second time and no before.
- "add records exactly the elab_term it returns" doesn't hold under `autolabel_singleton_tuple` (the singleton-label lifting at the end of `uexp_to_info_map`): it stores the inner elaboration at the source ids but returns a different term.

Something like one comment per binding, each saying what the value is:

```reason
/* The expanded Let analyzed a self-referencing definition recursively,
   with the module's name in scope; modules are not recursive, so that
   analysis can't be reused. */
let names_itself = …;
/* The definition's elaboration before the Let wraps it, as recorded in
   its info (except under sing
items.evidence: fa3eef62ce "Comments say what the code does, one per binding"; matthewhammer replied 4340596675 "Done in fa3eef62ce".

items.text:
🤖 Option 2: accept the stuck result. A bare value under a module signature should be stuck *and* a static error. modules-ii/1-sig-types already does both: signatures are `Typ.Sig` there, so the singleton-label lift never runs, and `module M : { let x : Int } = 5 in M.x` reports "Expecting type { let x:Int } but got inconsistent type Int" and evaluates to `(5:({ let x:Int })).x`, with or without this PR. On dev the missing error is temporary, so no special case is needed here.

For the test you proposed for this program: either pin it as stuck with a note that the static error comes with Modules II part 1, or leave it out of this PR and add it on part 1, where it can assert both the stuck term and the error.
items.evidence: matthewhammer replied 4340771544: "Agreed, option 2: no special case here. The test for this program goes on Modules II part 1". No pushback.
items.what_is_left: The promised test lives on Modules II part 1, not here.

items.text:
🤖 `names_itself` also matches a fixpoint the user wrote. `module m = fix f -> fun x -> … f(x - 1) in m(3)` elaborates to `Let(_, FixF(…), _)` because `fix` itself elaborates to a `FixF`, so the read-back is skipped and the definition is analyzed twice. On modules-ii part 1 with this PR merged, a temporary print in this match fired for every `module … = fix …` I tried (four programs) and not for a `fix` inside a module body. The results match dev, so it's only the speedup that's lost. But the check doesn't actually test what `names_itself` claims to.

Telling the two apart from the elaboration's shape is hard. "Skip when the definition is a `fix`" would also skip `module m = fix g -> fun x -> … m(x - 1)`, which currently gets its unbound-`m` error from the fallback. That suggests the signal belongs in the `Let` analysis itself: an argument that makes a module binding non-recursive, as in your report's "what next". There'd be no shape check and no fallback, and `fix` would still be how a module binds a recursive function. That change can be a follow-up if you'd prefer to keep this PR small.

This also depends on https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/pull/2651#discussion_r4340431274. If

| `5a52` | Expecting `x=Int`, got `x=x=Int, y=Int` in `x={ … }` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `6053` | same as `4f52` | ✓ | — |
| `6b53` | same as `5a52` | ✓ | — |
